records.context: Design rules:
records.label: spacr.crashreport#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Design rules:
records.translation: Designregler:

records.context: **Collectors do not throw.** Every collector executes through :func:`_collect`, which turns a failure into a manifest entry naming what could not be gathered and why. Catching ``Exception`` is acceptable here because the failure is recorded in the output: the manifest is part of the bundle, so a missing section is visible to the report recipient instead of silently absent.
records.label: spacr.crashreport#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Collectors do not raise.** Every collector runs through :func:`_collect`, which turns a failure into a manifest entry naming what could not be gathered and why. Catching ``Exception`` is acceptable here because the failure is recorded in the output: the manifest is part of the bundle, so a missing section is visible to the report recipient instead of silently absent.
records.translation: **Insamlare utlöser inga fel.** Varje insamlare körs genom :func:`_collect`, som gör om ett fel till en manifestpost som namnger vad som inte kunde samlas in och varför. Att fånga ``Exception`` är godtagbart här eftersom felet registreras i utdata: manifestet ingår i paketet, så att en saknad sektion syns för rapportens mottagare i stället för att tyst saknas.

records.context: **Bounded size.** ``spacr.log`` rotates but a single run can still write hundreds of megabytes. The bundle takes the *tail* of it, capped by :data:`MAX_LOG_BYTES`, and the manifest records how much was dropped.
records.label: spacr.crashreport#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Bounded size.** ``spacr.log`` rotates but a single run can still write hundreds of megabytes. The bundle takes the *tail* of it, capped by :data:`MAX_LOG_BYTES`, and the manifest records how much was dropped.
records.translation: **Begränsad storlek.** ``spacr.log`` roteras, men en enskild körning kan ändå skriva hundratals megabyte. Paketet tar *slutet* av den, begränsat av :data:`MAX_LOG_BYTES`, och manifestet registrerar hur mycket som utelämnades.

records.context: **Nothing secret.** Environment variables are included because ``SPACR_*``, ``CUDA_*`` and ``PATH`` explain a large fraction of "works here, not there" — but a value whose *name* looks like a credential is replaced with ``"<redacted>"`` and listed by name in the manifest, so you can see what was withheld and the report recipient can see that something was. Absolute paths are kept: they name the checkout, the plate and the database, and a report with them stripped cannot be acted on.
records.label: spacr.crashreport#8
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Nothing secret.** Environment variables are included because ``SPACR_*``, ``CUDA_*`` and ``PATH`` explain a large fraction of "works here, not there" — but a value whose *name* looks like a credential is replaced with ``"<redacted>"`` and listed by name in the manifest, so you can see what was withheld and the report recipient can see that something was. Absolute paths are kept: they name the checkout, the plate and the database, and a report with them stripped cannot be acted on.

records.context: The module also sets the starting form of every graph in spaCR. The Default Graph Type preference is stored per data shape (`spacr.qt.preferences`), read back through :func:`chosen_for`, and turned into the graph drawn before the first right-click by :func:`default_for` and :func:`start_for`. Their answer accounts for the user's choice, whether that choice fits the data, and whether there are enough observations to support it, so every new graph applies the preference without extra code.

Denna modul sätter samman dessa länkar till ett träd, så att en fråga som "cell 41 in field 3 has one nucleus and four pathogens, and one of those pathogens has an area that would be impossible inside that nucleus" kan besvaras genom att en cell inspekteras.

records.context: Why a tree and not a join
records.label: spacr.lineage#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Why a tree and not a join
records.translation: Varför ett träd och inte en sammanfogning

records.context: A join answers "give me every pathogen with its cell's area". A tree answers "what is inside this cell", which is a different question and the one a person looking at an extracted image region actually has. The difference shows up in the failures: a join silently drops a cell with no pathogens and silently drops a pathogen whose ``cell_id`` names a cell that is not there. Both of those are findings — the first is the negative control working, the second is a segmentation bug — so :func:`build_forest` keeps childless parents and :func:`orphans` returns the unattached children rather than discarding them.
records.label: spacr.lineage#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A join answers "give me every pathogen with its cell's area". A tree answers "what is inside this cell", which is a different question and the one a person looking at a crop actually has. The difference shows up in the failures: a join silently drops a cell with no pathogens and silently drops a pathogen whose ``cell_id`` names a cell that is not there. Both of those are findings — the first is the negative control working, the second is a segmentation bug — so :func:`build_forest` keeps childless parents and :func:`orphans` returns the unattached children rather than discarding them.
records.translation: En sammanfogning besvarar "give me every pathogen with its cell's area". Ett träd besvarar "what is inside this cell", vilket är en annan fråga och den som en person som tittar på ett utklipp faktiskt har. Skillnaden syns i felen: en sammanfogning tar tyst bort en cell utan patogener och tar tyst bort en patogen vars ``cell_id`` namnger en cell som inte finns. Båda dessa är fynd — det första är den negativa kontrollen som fungerar, det andra är en segmenteringsbugg — så :func:`build_forest` behåller föräldrar utan barn och :func:`orphans` returnerar de ofästa barnen i stället för att förkasta dem.

records.context: Tree nodes use :func:`spacr.selection.object_keys`. The same identifier appears in three views: UMAP, the plate view, and the crop grid. Selecting a tree node therefore publishes an identifier understood by all three. Resolve each child's parent *only inside its own field*. ``cell_id`` is a label rather than a unique key; label 7 can appear in each field.

records.source: Nodes are keyed by :func:`spacr.selection.object_keys`, the same string the UMAP, the plate view and the crop grid use, so selecting a node in the tree publishes something every other view already understands. A child's parent is resolved *within its own field*: ``cell_id`` is a label, not a key, and label 7 exists in every field on the plate.
records.translation: Noder nycklas med :func:`spacr.selection.object_keys`, samma sträng som UMAP, plattvyn och utklippsrutnätet använder, så att val av en nod i trädet publicerar något som varje annan vy redan förstår. Ett barns förälder löses upp *inom dess eget bildfält*: ``cell_id`` är en etikett, inte en nyckel, och etikett 7 finns i varje bildfält på plattan.

records.source: :data:`spacr.selection.OBJECT_KEY_COLUMNS` used to be the field plus the object label, with no table in it, so a nucleus labelled 1 and a pathogen labelled 1 in the same field had **the same key**. A lineage tree is where that became visible, because a cell's own children are exactly the objects most likely to collide: four objects opened as three crops and which one you got depended on the row order of ``png_list``.
records.translation: :data:`spacr.selection.OBJECT_KEY_COLUMNS` brukade vara bildfältet plus objektetiketten, utan tabell, så att en cellkärna med etikett 1 och en patogen med etikett 1 i samma bildfält hade **samma nyckel**. records.context: :func:`spacr.selection.object_keys` now writes the object type into the structured-data name, so a node's shared structured-data name already says which table it came from and :attr:`LineageNode.node_id` is the same identity in a different spelling. Both are kept. ``node_id`` is what the tree addresses its rows by and cannot collide by construction; :meth:`LineageNode.key_collisions` compares the two and is now a **regression test rather than a warning** — it finds nothing on a correctly keyed forest, and :func:`build_forest` still takes ``typed=False`` so the collapse can be reproduced on demand rather than only remembered.

records.source: :func:`spacr.selection.object_keys` now writes the object type into the key, so a node's shared key already says which table it came from and :attr:`LineageNode.node_id` is the same identity in a different spelling. Both are kept. ``node_id`` is what the tree addresses its rows by and cannot collide by construction; :meth:`LineageNode.key_collisions` compares the two and is now a **regression test rather than a warning** — it finds nothing on a correctly keyed forest, and :func:`build_forest` still takes ``typed=False`` so the collapse can be reproduced on demand rather than only remembered.
records.translation: :func:`spacr.selection.object_keys` skriver nu objekttypen i nyckeln, så att en nods gemensamma nyckel redan säger vilken tabell den kom från och :attr:`LineageNode.node_id` är samma identitet i en annan stavning. Att slå samman de två skulle rapportera en kollision på varje platta.

records.source: These are not seven more entries in the regression_type menu. records.translation: Detta är inte sju poster till i menyn regression_type. De anpassningar som spaCR redan erbjuder ger alla samma utdata -- en koefficient per guide, med ett standardfel och ett P-värde -- och resten av screenen bygger på det: vulkandiagrammet ritar effekt mot signifikans, träfflistan rangordnar gener efter effekt med ett q över de testade generna, och tillskrivningen och modellkortet använder samma tabell.

records.context: What each method fits is not always the guide design. spaCR's fit is guide -> phenotype at microplate sample position level with one column per guide: high dimensional, sparse and categorical, which is the worst case for most of these. Against a continuous covariate -- guide abundance in the microplate sample position, cell count, laboratory microplate position -- they are microplate sample position suited, and the smoothers are used there: showing whether the phenotype moves smoothly with a nuisance variable the linear model is assuming away.
records.label: spacr.nonparametric_fits#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: What each method fits is not always the guide design. spaCR's fit is guide -> phenotype at well level with one column per guide: high dimensional, sparse and categorical, which is the worst case for most of these. Against a continuous covariate -- guide abundance in the well, cell count, plate position -- they are well suited, and the smoothers are used there: showing whether the phenotype moves smoothly with a nuisance variable the linear model is assuming away.
records.translation: Det som varje metod anpassar är inte alltid guidedesignen. spaCR:s anpassning är guide -> fenotyp på brunnsnivå med en kolumn per guide: högdimensionell, gles och kategorisk, vilket är det värsta fallet för de flesta av dessa. Mot en kontinuerlig kovariat -- guideförekomst i brunnen, cellantal, plattposition -- passar de väl, och utjämnarna används där: för att visa om fenotypen rör sig jämnt med en störvariabel som den linjära modellen antar bort.

records.context: The result also reports how many nuclei agree, which the triangle consensus does not. `align_by_triangles` returned a transform for every pair it was given, including phenotype microscope image fields and sequencing microscope image fields from opposite sides of the microplate sample position, because three coincidentally similar triangles can always be found in two sets of a few hundred points. records.translation: Resultatet rapporterar också hur många cellkärnor som stämmer överens, vilket triangelkonsensus inte gör. `align_by_triangles` returnerade en transformation för varje par den fick, inklusive fenotyprutor och sekvenseringsrutor från motsatta sidor av brunnen, eftersom tre tillfälligt likartade trianglar alltid kan hittas i två mängder med några hundra punkter. records.context: This complements the triangle consensus, which estimates the scale and on sparse or noisy correspondence estimates it poorly -- 0.36 where the truth was 0.25, measured. records.source: This complements the triangle consensus, which estimates the scale and on sparse or noisy correspondence estimates it poorly -- 0.36 where the truth was 0.25, measured. Refinement cannot recover from that: a transform that far off finds a small self-consistent cluster of points near its own fixed point and converges onto it. The scale does not need to be estimated, because it is the ratio of the two acquisitions' tile pitches, which the layout provides.
records.translation: Detta kompletterar triangelkonsensus, som skattar skalan och vid gles eller brusig korrespondens skattar den dåligt -- 0.36 där sanningen var 0.25, uppmätt. Förfining kan inte återhämta sig från det: en transformation som ligger så långt fel hittar ett litet självkonsistent kluster av punkter nära sin egen fixpunkt och konvergerar mot det. Skalan behöver inte skattas, eftersom den är kvoten mellan de två insamlingarnas rutavstånd, som layouten tillhandahåller.

records.context: So this fixes the scale and searches only rotation and translation, which two matched points determine exactly. records.translation: Därför fixerar detta skalan och söker endast rotation och translation, som två matchade punkter bestämmer exakt. records.context: Nuclei at 10X are round blobs. They have no corners, so a corner detector finds essentially nothing and the matcher's scores are noise. Phase correlation asks a different question -- what single translation makes these two microscope fields of view agree -- and a microscope field of view of blobs answers it very well. Feature matching is still used in one other place: the phenotype-to-SBS step across magnifications, where scale and rotation are real.

records.source: Nuclei at 10X are round blobs. They have no corners, so a corner detector finds essentially nothing and the matcher's scores are noise. Phase correlation asks a different question -- what single translation makes these two fields agree -- and a field of blobs answers it very well. Feature matching is still used in one other place: the phenotype-to-SBS step across magnifications, where scale and rotation are real.
records.translation: Cellkärnor vid 10X är runda klumpar. De har inga hörn, så en hörndetektor hittar i stort sett ingenting och matcharens poäng är brus. Faskorrelation ställer en annan fråga -- vilken enda translation som får dessa två bildfält att stämma överens -- och ett bildfält av klumpar besvarar den mycket väl. Egenskapsmatchning används fortfarande på ett annat ställe: steget från fenotyp till SBS över förstoringar, där skala och rotation är verkliga.

records.context: The shift comes back wrapped. An FFT has no notion of which way is negative: a -213 px shift of a 1480 px microscope image field arrives as +1267. records.source: The shift comes back wrapped. An FFT has no notion of which way is negative: a -213 px shift of a 1480 px tile arrives as +1267. records.translation: Förskjutningen kommer tillbaka omlindad. En FFT har ingen uppfattning om vilket håll som är negativt: en förskjutning på -213 px i en ruta på 1480 px kommer som +1267. Att läsa den utan att linda upp den gav felaktiga förskjutningar i en tidig prototyp även om varje enskild registrering var korrekt. :func:`unwrap` viker allt bortom en halv ruta in i den negativa halvan.

records.source: Versioned extension SDK for third-party spaCR plugins.

records.context: Plugins are ordinary Python distributions exposing one entry point in the ``spacr.plugins`` group.  The entry point may resolve to a :class:`SpacrPlugin`, a mapping accepted by :func:`plugin_from_mapping`, or a zero-argument factory returning either.  Discovery is lazy, deterministic and failure-isolated: one malformed plugin is recorded in :func:`diagnostics` without preventing spaCR or the remaining plugins from loading.
records.label: spacr.plugins#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Plugins are ordinary Python distributions exposing one entry point in the ``spacr.plugins`` group.  The entry point may resolve to a :class:`SpacrPlugin`, a mapping accepted by :func:`plugin_from_mapping`, or a zero-argument factory returning either.  Discovery is lazy, deterministic and failure-isolated: one malformed plugin is recorded in :func:`diagnostics` without preventing spaCR or the remaining plugins from loading.
records.translation: Insticksprogram är vanliga Python-distributioner som exponerar en ingångspunkt i gruppen ``spacr.plugins``. Ingångspunkten kan lösas upp till ett :class:`SpacrPlugin`, en avbildning som godtas av :func:`plugin_from_mapping` eller en fabrik utan argument som returnerar något av dem. Identifieringen är lat, deterministisk och felisolerad: ett felaktigt insticksprogram registreras i :func:`diagnostics` utan att hindra spaCR eller de återstående insticksprogrammen från att läsas in.

records.context: This measures an ENCODING fault rather than a drawing one. Saving a GIF with ``disposal=2`` tells a decoder to clear each frame to the background colour before drawing the next; when the encoder then optimises a frame down to the sub-rectangle that actually changed, everything outside that rectangle is left showing the background. The animation plays with a bright ring flashing around it once per loop, and Qt's ``QMovie`` renders it exactly as described -- this was measured through the GUI path, not inferred from the file.
records.label: spacr.setting_animations.measure_border_artifact#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: This measures an ENCODING fault rather than a drawing one. Saving a GIF with ``disposal=2`` tells a decoder to clear each frame to the background colour before drawing the next; when the encoder then optimises a frame down to the sub-rectangle that actually changed, everything outside that rectangle is left showing the background. The animation plays with a bright ring flashing around it once per loop, and Qt's ``QMovie`` renders it exactly as described -- this was measured through the GUI path, not inferred from the file.
records.translation: Detta mäter ett KODNINGSFEL snarare än ett ritfel. Att spara en GIF med ``disposal=2`` säger åt en avkodare att rensa varje bildruta till bakgrundsfärgen innan nästa ritas; när kodaren sedan optimerar en bildruta ned till den delrektangel som faktiskt ändrades lämnas allt utanför den rektangeln med bakgrunden synlig. Animationen spelas med en ljus ring som blinkar runt den en gång per slinga, och Qt:s ``QMovie`` återger den exakt så som beskrivet -- detta mättes genom GUI-vägen, inte härlett från filen.
